title: Context and requirements
caption: A useful but incomplete analogy: both ask what information supports the work, but an agent's context is not a requirements document.
label: The board inside the context window, with static and dynamic context beside it

the-claim.title: The claim
the-claim.script: Here is a useful analogy, not an equivalence: context engineering has something in common with requirements engineering. Both ask what information supports the work. But an agent's context is a limited, changing set of information, and may include material retrieved while it works; it is not simply a requirements document.

the-route.title: The route
the-route.script: The route has four stops. First, what the AI sees: think of the context window as the desk the AI works at. Then static and dynamic context: what is set up before work starts, and what may be retrieved while it runs. Next, how context can go wrong, and finally, ways to keep it useful.
